# Reference trace captured from the real Lua `game/online/match_driver.lua`,
# driving a scripted sequence that forces a rollback: the star (a real
# `game/transport/fake_star.lua` pair from
# `game/online/match_driver_fixture.lua`'s `fixture.session("1v1")`) only
# pumps every 5 steps, so both peers predict the rows they have not received
# and correct them in one burst once the pump runs — the same `run_bursty`
# shape `spec/game/online_match_driver_spec.lua` uses to exercise rollback.
# This vector is frozen and cannot be regenerated: the Lua implementation it
# was captured from no longer exists in this repository. A failing
# differential against it is a finding about the Rust or TypeScript code
# under test, not a fixture to refresh. See tools/lua_reference/README.md
# for provenance.
#
# `rollback`/`correction` are `RollbackSessionDiagnostics.rollback_count`/
# `.correction_count` and only move at a pump step, confirming the burst
# shape actually predicted and then corrected. `hash <step> <peer> <tick>
# <digest>` lines are `match_snapshot.hash` at each 10-tick checkpoint; host
# and guest agree at every one (10, 20, ..., 90) — this is the real Lua
# proving out the exact claim the port needs to reproduce bit for bit.
#
# Regenerated 2026-08-06, and the reason matters. The first note here said the
# old trace had "drifted from the current real Lua" after Rust-side fixes
# landed. That cannot happen: the Lua tree is pristine and Rust changes cannot
# alter Lua output. The real cause is that the original capture advanced each
# driver with a `nil` sample, where `spec/game/online_match_driver_spec.lua`'s
# `run_bursty` uses `input_frame.neutral_sample()` — a `nil` sample yields
# degenerate `nil` diagnostics throughout. So the HARNESS was wrong, not the
# reference. Independently re-captured from pristine Lua with a harness written
# from the spec: all 18 checkpoint hashes matched this file exactly.
#
# Original note, kept because the symptom it describes was real — `crate::match_driver`'s
# Rust port matched the *old* trace exactly through the first rollback and
# then diverged from `correction_count` onward, which pointed at a stale
# fixture rather than a Rust defect. A fresh capture from the current Lua,
# using this file's own documented regeneration recipe, reproduced the
# Rust port's numbers exactly, tick for tick and hash for hash, confirming
# the port was correct and the committed fixture was the thing that had
# gone stale. This file is that fresh capture.
#
# `crates/gc-netcode/tests/match_driver.rs`'s
# `match_driver_differential_matches_the_lua_reference` builds the identical
# scenario through `gc_netcode::match_driver`/`gc_netcode::match_driver_fixture`
# and asserts its `diagnostics()`/`checkpoints()` match this trace tick for
# tick — no longer `#[ignore]`d.
#
